message.content: Confirmed—the flagged case fails the yellow-duration check at step 468. I'll shrink it to a minimal reproduction and trace the signal timing to isolate the cause.
Shrinking isolated a minimal case that still violates the yellow timing with just 205 steps. Now I'll replay it and examine the signal state around the failure point to confirm the timing truncation.
The trace shows the yellow phase was cut to 3 seconds because the run ended mid-cycle. I'll test a counterfactual with a longer duration to verify the timing holds when the simulation can complete.
That extra time didn't fix it – the controller itself is ending the yellow early after just 3 seconds. I'll check whether switching to fixed-time control prevents the early termination.
My previous analysis identified the root cause as actuated control truncating yellow early — switching to fixed-time eliminates the violation. I'll now file the formal report with the full evidence.
